On May 9, 2026 , the Premier League witnessed a tactical chess match as Liverpool hosted Chelsea in a fixture filled with intensity and high-profile talent. Both sides entered the pitch looking for a decisive result in one of the season's most anticipated showdowns. Gravenberch Strikes Early and Enzo Responds The match began in electric fashion, with Liverpool seizing control in the opening minutes. In the 6th minute, the early pressure paid off: following key passes from Milos Kerkez and the young Rio Ngumoha , Ryan Gravenberch unleashed a powerful right-footed strike from outside the box, beating the keeper to open the scoring. The stadium erupted, and the home side nearly doubled their lead shortly after when a defensive blunder by Filip Joergensen almost resulted in a costly goal. However, Chelsea refused to be rattled and began to find their rhythm through possession. The visitors' response arrived in the 35th minute through a moment of pure technical class. Enzo Fernandez stepped up for a direct free kick and curled a magnificent right-footed shot into the back of the net, restoring parity before the halftime whistle. The balance was restored, with both teams demonstrating why they remain at the sharp end of the table. VAR Dominates a Tense Second Half The second half was defined by a series of VAR interventions that dictated the emotional flow of the game. In the 49th minute, Chelsea thought they had completed the comeback when Cole Palmer found the net, but after a lengthy review, the goal was disallowed due to an offside call against Marc Cucurella . The frustration shifted to the other side soon after as Liverpool had two separate penalty shouts—in the 60th and 79th minutes—turned down by the referee following on-field monitor reviews. In the closing stages, tension reached a boiling point as tactical substitutions saw Alexander Isak and Federico Chiesa introduced for the Reds. Late in the 89th minute, it was Chelsea's turn to face a nervous wait for a potential penalty, but the referee once again stood by his original decision. Amidst a flurry of yellow cards for the likes of Moises Caicedo and Alexis Mac Allister , the contest ended in a hard-fought draw where technology and talent shared center stage.

matches.title: Chelsea FC vs Nottingham Forest
matches.description: Watch Chelsea vs Nottingham Forest highlights and goals from Premier League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 4, 2026. On May 4, 2026 , the atmosphere at Stamford Bridge reached a fever pitch as Chelsea welcomed Nottingham Forest for a Premier League clash. The visitors wasted little time in signaling their intent, stunning the home crowd almost immediately after the opening whistle. Forest Strike Early and Often It took just two minutes for the deadlock to be broken. A precise ball from Dilane Bakwa found Taiwo Awoniyi , who expertly headed home to put Nottingham Forest in the driving seat. The early goal rattled the hosts, and the situation deteriorated further for Chelsea when Malo Gusto was cautioned for a shirt pull on Awoniyi inside the box. After a tense VAR check confirmed the infringement, Igor Jesus stepped up to the penalty spot in the 15th minute and coolly converted, sending Robert Sanchez the wrong way to double the advantage. Chelsea looked to respond with intensity, and they came agonizingly close when Enzo Fernandez rattled the post shortly before the half-hour mark. Despite waves of pressure and a series of corners, Chelsea struggled to unlock the visiting defense. Their frustrations peaked just before the interval when Zach Abbott conceded a penalty for a foul on Jesse Derry . However, Cole Palmer was unable to capitalize on the opportunity, as his spot-kick was brilliantly blocked by the goalkeeper, sending the visitors into the break with a commanding lead. Tactical Shifts and Second-Half Drama Returning from the tunnel for the second half, both managers opted for personnel changes, with Morgan Gibbs-White and Elliot Anderson introduced for the visitors. The impact was immediate. In the 52nd minute, Gibbs-White provided the delivery for Awoniyi , who tapped in his second of the match to extend the Nottingham Forest lead to 3-0. The goal survived a lengthy VAR review, confirming the visitors' dominance and leaving the Chelsea faithful silent. Desperate to find a lifeline, Chelsea intensified their pursuit in the final stages. Their persistent attacking paid off in the 73rd minute when they appeared to have pulled a goal back, only for the referee to rule it out for offside after a VAR intervention. The intensity of the contest spilled over into the 78th minute as Moises Caicedo and Liam Delap were both shown yellow cards following a heated exchange. In the dying embers of the match, Chelsea finally broke their duck. In the 93rd minute, Marc Cucurella provided the assist for Joao Pedro , who produced a stunning bicycle-kick to find the back of the net. While the goal injected a spark of hope, time ultimately ran out for the hosts. Nottingham Forest held firm against a late surge, cementing a clinical performance in front of 39,605 fans to secure all three points.

matches.title: Chelsea FC vs Leeds
matches.description: Watch Chelsea vs Leeds highlights and goals from FA Cup on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on April 26, 2026. Enzo Fernandez’s clinical first-half header proved the difference as Chelsea ground out a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Leeds United in the FA Cup. On a high-stakes afternoon at Stamford Bridge on April 26, 2026, the Blues combined flashes of brilliance with defensive grit to overcome their resilient visitors in a match that simmered with tension until the final whistle. First Half: Chelsea Strike After Woodwork Scare The contest began with both sides searching for rhythm, though Leeds nearly snatched an early lead when Ao Tanaka’s direct free kick sailed just wide of the target. Chelsea gradually asserted dominance, controlling 55% of the ball, but they were almost caught out in the 22nd minute. Joao Pedro found himself with a golden chance , only to see his effort rattle the post and bounce clear. That scare served as a wake-up call. Just one minute later, the deadlock was broken. Exploiting a defensive error from Pascal Struijk, Pedro Neto delivered a pinpoint cross into the danger zone. Enzo Fernandez reacted quickest, guiding a powerful header home to record the opening goal of the match . While Joao Pedro’s playmaking proved vital in the build-up, it was Fernandez’s composure that gave the home side the advantage heading into the break. Second Half: Leeds Pressure and Tactical Shifts The second half saw Leeds United emerge with renewed intent. Managerial shifts at the interval saw Joe Rodon and Anton Stach introduced to stabilize the visitors, and they nearly found an equalizer in the 58th minute. Dominic Calvert-Lewin connected with a goal-bound header, but Chelsea keeper Robert Sanchez was well-positioned to make a comfortable save. Chelsea looked to regain control by introducing Cole Palmer and Andrey Santos. Palmer’s arrival added a creative spark, though the football on display became increasingly physical as the minutes ticked down. Both teams struggled with accuracy in the final third, with Tanaka and Stach both seeing efforts fly off-target as the Leeds frustration began to mount. Late Drama and Disciplinary Firefight The final twenty minutes of the sports spectacle were defined by a flurry of cautions as the referee struggled to maintain order. Moises Caicedo, Cole Palmer, and Pedro Neto all saw yellow for Chelsea, while Leeds players Struijk, Ethan Ampadu, Lukas Nmecha, and Jayden Bogle were also booked in a frantic period of play. Despite a late barrage of long throws into the Chelsea box and a nervous defensive blunder by Ampadu that nearly cost Leeds further, the Blues' backline held firm. Tosin Adarabioyo and Trevoh Chalobah provided crucial clearances in stoppage time, while Sanchez commanded his area to intercept a late cross. When the final whistle blew, Chelsea’s narrow lead remained intact, securing their progression in the competition after a bruising encounter.

The breakthrough arrived in the 25th minute following a moment of technical brilliance. The goal gave the home side a deserved lead and left Chelsea searching for answers as they struggled to break through a resilient defensive line before the interval. Drama and a Turning Point After the Break The second half began in chaotic fashion for the Londoners. In the 50th minute, disaster struck for the visitors when Malo Gusto inadvertently turned the ball into his own net, doubling Sunderland 's advantage. Chelsea responded swiftly to the setback, as Cole Palmer clinical finish from outside the box pulled a goal back in the 56th minute following an assist from Pedro Neto . However, the momentum shifted back to the hosts just six minutes later when Wesley Fofana received a second yellow card and was sent off, leaving the visitors to fight the remainder of the contest with ten men. Resilient Defense Secures the Win As the clock ticked down, the match became increasingly physical, with the referee issuing several cautions to maintain control. Players including Enzo Fernandez , Granit Xhaka , and Habib Diarra all saw yellow as tensions flared. Despite tactical substitutions from both managers, including the introduction of Liam Delap for Chelsea and Chris Rigg for Sunderland , the scoreline remained unchanged. Robert Sanchez made a few late claims to keep his side in the hunt, but Sunderland held firm to secure a 2-1 victory, navigating through 14 minutes of stoppage time to claim all three points.
